profile.headline: Independent AI Safety and Alignment Researcher | Professional software developer | Argues with Claude for a living
profile.summary:
I build software for a living, and I build trust in AI because someone has to.
 
By day, I'm a Software Engineer on the platform development team at NISC, where our payments platform serves cooperative members across the country. It's heavily regulated work, and I love that. Regulated environments teach you a discipline most engineers never get: every decision has to survive scrutiny, and "it works" is never the whole story.
 
That discipline is exactly what I bring to the work I care about most.
 
Through Windrose and Company, I help schools, small businesses, freelancers, and solopreneurs adopt AI responsibly and with confidence. Last year, I worked with my daughter's rural K-8 district to author their AI policy from the ground up. Their legal team reviewed it; their board adopted it without a single edit. I still come back every fall to train staff, parents, and students, and I'm proud to say that our tiny rural school is in many ways far more prepared than even some of the largest and best-funded districts in the nation at this time. Making our smallness an advantage, not a weakness, is also deeply important to me.
 
Beyond simply advising on these systems, I run them. I maintain ai.windrose.dev in my spare time as a free and open home for AI safety research and educator resources. I run my own local AI infrastructure from the hardware up, and I'm completing a Computer Science degree at Maryville University with a focus on AI. I advise on AI systems because I am equal parts enamored with the promise of what they could be and frustrated with how they fall short of that, and I believe the difference is in the care we take to educate ourselves and others, and to handle this technology responsibly and equitably.
 
Here's what I believe: the people building and deploying AI should be the ones most worried about it going wrong. Not the loudest optimists. The careful ones.
 
I help eliminate the confusion and risk in AI. I make AI a safe investment.
 
If you lead a school, run a small business, or are a solopreneur trying to figure out what AI means for you, my door is open. Reach out. I like it when people bring me problems - I exist to make life easier for others.

positions.title: Co-Founder
positions.description:
My wife and I founded Windrose because we believe that great people should run great businesses and that great businesses can solve the world's problems.

With that in mind, we set out to leverage our combined - and extraordinarily diverse - skill sets to help empower small businesses to get bigger in ways that are:
- sustainable
- profitable
- ethical
- enjoyable

At Windrose, our work is informed by experience in some of the most successful organizations in the world; we've worked for companies as big as Nordstrom, Starbucks, and the Four Seasons, and for companies as small as "One of the top commercial realtors in Missouri" and "The most successful strings shop in St. Louis". Every step of the way, we have obsessively studied what made great businesses thrive and other businesses fail. 

From those lessons, we learned:
1) Businesses succeed for two reasons, and neither is their product or service. Those reasons are people and systems. Great people, empowered to focus only on what they are good at and passionate about, and their work is informed and amplified by efficient, intuitive, scalable systems. When you do this well, you can sell anything, you can sell to anyone, and you can likely make it profitable

2) In order to feel empowered, humans need to be freed from the things that drag them down. Repetitive processes and "figuring out what to do" are the two greatest enemies to efficiency and empowerment in a business. With the right processes and systems, people sore. Without them, time and resources are wasted, people feel ineffective, excitement dies, and culture is soon to follow. Culture drive all things - we are a culture-first consultancy.

3) Without data, you are guessing. Without accurate data, you are hypothesizing. When you have accurate data, you can plan, act, assess, and adapt as needed. As long as you can do those 4 things effectively and efficiently, your business is effectively immortal.

These lessons define everything we do.
positions.insights: Skills: Business Process Improvement · Digital Strategy · Enterprise Software · Start-up Leadership · Web Application Development · Programming · Content Management Systems (CMS) · Business Process · Leadership · JavaScript · Software Testing

positions.title: Program Manager - Full Stack
positions.description:
As Program Manager for the Full Stack Web Development program at Savvy Coders, I've had the extraordinary opportunity to:
- impact student learning experience by continuing to teach personally in each cohort, learning each students strengths, weaknesses, and goals; learning how THEY learn and meeting them where they are
- impact student outcomes by giving them the confidence and intangible tools necessary to excel in development work and in the workplace at large
- impact families' lives by helping applicants find the confidence and the skills necessary to step into a tech career that was inaccessible prior. I've gotten to see grads buy their first house or pay for their first kid's college with money they made on these skills.
- Step into a community outreach role, getting to meet change makers and NPOs throughout the region, leading to partnerships valued well beyond the scope of my work at Savvy
- Step into a business process architect role and design, implement, and iterate on automations, systems, curriculum management, and data management that helped empower the organization to grow our reach beyond STL. We have since graduated students from Hawaii to eastern Africa!
- Write curriculum from scratch, from written materials to hands on exercises, code examples, and video walk-throughs. I learned video editing, social media management, and much more... an invaluable education I was fortunate enough to get paid for pursuing. I live for learning, and this has been a particularly engaging challenge!

I added to the length and depth of our testing/QA modules, helped to coach the Data Analytics with Python team toward a more sustainable, scalable model that better aligned with the other systems, assisted with data migrations and system upgrades and instituted new tracking.

Every day on this job has been a new adventure and I've absorbed every new thing possible along the way while changing lives all along - ideal stuff. ♥

positions.title: Instructor
positions.description:
I was honored with the opportunity to return to Savvy Coders after the completion of the April 2021 Full Stack Web Development Bootcamp as a teaching assistant for the next FS cohort. 

As a TA, I served as first point of contact and primary resource for 3 students in the current program, helping to guide them through the experience, answer questions, provide outside resources, and help to ensure generally that they remain on track, have a positive experience, and come out the other side as well rounded, clean coding problem solvers!

Subsequently I was asked to take over teaching the Thursday review nights, which was richly fulfilling. The thrill of seeing a student (who'd struggled with a topic during the week) finally reach clarity was an incredible feeling. 

After a short break (during my tenure at Leidos, I was hired back full time to manage the program, and continued to teach to keep engaged with the student body and help inform efforts to continuously update and improve on our curriculum.

projects.title: Threat Map
projects.description:
ThreatMap is a cybersecurity dashboard that visualizes global malicious IP activity using real-time threat intelligence data. The app integrates live data from Open Threat Exchange (OTX) pulses and AbuseIPDB reports to generate interactive visualizations, including a geographic heatmap of threat concentration and a detailed drill-down for individual IPs. Built with a focus on clarity, speed, and extensibility, ThreatMap showcases skills in data engineering, API integration, and visual storytelling for security analysis.

Live Dashboard: https://threatmap.streamlit.app 

GitHub Repo:
https://github.com/drod1107/threatmap
